# select_databricks_connection (Resource)

A connection to one Databricks account: the workspace SELECT reads through, the SQL warehouse it runs its queries on, and the service principal it authenticates as.

## About

A Databricks connection is how SELECT reads one Databricks account's usage and spend: the workspace it connects through, the SQL warehouse it runs its queries on, and the service principal it authenticates as. To learn more, see the [SELECT documentation](https://select.dev/docs/getting-started).

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API. The `api_key` configured on the provider must carry the `databricks_connections:read` and `databricks_connections:write` scopes; without them every operation fails with an authorization error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# SELECT reads a Databricks account's usage through one workspace per region.
# The service principal is an OAuth machine-to-machine identity with access to
# the workspace's SQL warehouse and read access to the account's system tables.
resource "select_databricks_connection" "production_us_east" {
  name = "Acme Production (us-east-1)"

  databricks_account_id = "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"
  primary_workspace_url = "https://acme-prod.cloud.databricks.com"
  warehouse_id          = "abc123def4567890"

  credentials = {
    client_id     = "88888888-9999-aaaa-bbbb-cccccccccccc"
    client_secret = var.databricks_client_secret
  }
}

# One account can have several connections, one per region, each reading through
# a workspace in its own region. SELECT allows one connection per account per
# region, so this is how an account spanning regions is covered.
resource "select_databricks_connection" "production_eu_west" {
  name = "Acme Production (eu-west-1)"

  databricks_account_id = "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"
  primary_workspace_url = "https://acme-prod-eu.cloud.databricks.com"
  warehouse_id          = "fedcba0987654321"

  credentials = {
    client_id     = "88888888-9999-aaaa-bbbb-cccccccccccc"
    client_secret = var.databricks_client_secret
  }

  # Sanitize query text before SELECT stores it, and hold off syncing until the
  # connection has been reviewed.
  query_sanitization_enabled = true
  sync_enabled               = false
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `credentials` (Attributes) The service principal SELECT authenticates as. The secret in this block is stored in a secret store and never returned by the API, so SELECT cannot detect changes made to it outside Terraform. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `databricks_account_id` (String) The Databricks account to read usage and spend for. Letters, digits and hyphens only.
- `name` (String) Display name for the connection, as shown throughout SELECT.
- `primary_workspace_url` (String) URL of the workspace to connect through, including the scheme — for example `https://my-workspace.cloud.databricks.com`. It must be in the region whose usage this connection should cover.
- `warehouse_id` (String) The SQL warehouse in that workspace to run queries on. Letters, digits and hyphens only.

### Optional

- `query_sanitization_enabled` (Boolean) Whether query text is sanitized before SELECT stores it.
- `sync_enabled` (Boolean) Whether SELECT starts syncing data for this connection.

### Read-Only

- `added_by_email` (String) Email address of the person who added the connection. Null when it was not added by a person.
- `connection_id` (String) Identifier of the connection resource this Databricks connection belongs to (see `GET /v2/connections/{connection_id}`). Distinct from `id`, which identifies this Databricks connection specifically.
- `create_time` (String) When the connection was added.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this connection. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The connection's identifier in SELECT, assigned when it is added. Use it with `terraform import` to bring an existing connection under management.
- `last_successful_sync_time` (String) When SELECT last completed a sync for this connection. Null before the first one succeeds.
- `metastore` (String) The Unity Catalog metastore this connection reads, in `cloud:region:id` form. Null until the first successful validation resolves it.
- `update_time` (String) When the connection was last changed.
- `workspace_ids` (List of String) The workspaces SELECT has found activity in for this account and region. Accumulated as they are discovered, so a workspace that has gone quiet stays listed. Empty until the first successful discovery.

### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Required:

- `client_id` (String) Client ID of the service principal SELECT authenticates as.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) An OAuth secret generated for that service principal.

## Import

`select_databricks_connection` can be imported using the connection's ID in SELECT:

```bash
terraform import select_databricks_connection.example 2f1c8b4e-9a6d-4d1f-9d0e-7d3a5b6c8e01
```

The ID is assigned by SELECT when the connection is added, so unlike a Snowflake account there is nothing about your Databricks setup that predicts it. It is the `id` attribute, and it is also the last path segment of the connection's page in the SELECT UI.

An import cannot recover `credentials`: SELECT stores the client secret in a secret store and returns neither half of the pair on this resource. Put the credentials in your configuration before importing, and the first apply after the import will re-send them — which makes SELECT revalidate the connection against Databricks.

## Additional Information

### One connection per account per region

SELECT reads a Databricks account through one workspace per region, and rejects a second connection covering the same ground. Two configurations are refused:

- a workspace whose Unity Catalog metastore is already connected, and
- a second connection for the same `databricks_account_id` in the same cloud and region.

Covering an account that spans regions means one resource per region, each pointing at a workspace in that region.

### Creating a connection validates it against Databricks

SELECT runs four checks in order — connectivity, workspace discovery, system table access, and metastore resolution — before it stores anything. A create that fails leaves no connection behind, and the error names the check that stopped the run along with what to change and the documentation page covering it. A check is only reported as `skipped` when an earlier one already failed.

This means `terraform apply` needs a service principal that actually works, and that a Databricks outage will fail the apply rather than store a broken connection.

### Which changes revalidate

SELECT revalidates whenever an apply changes `primary_workspace_url`, `warehouse_id` or `credentials`. Changing only `name`, `sync_enabled` or `query_sanitization_enabled` makes no call to Databricks, so a rename works even when Databricks does not.

A successful revalidation re-resolves `metastore` and adds any newly discovered workspaces to `workspace_ids`. That list accumulates and never shrinks: a workspace that has gone quiet stays listed.

### `databricks_account_id` cannot be changed

The account a connection reads is fixed when the connection is added. Changing it forces Terraform to destroy the connection and create a new one, which starts the account's usage history over.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the connection's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the connection changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.

The ETag also moves when the connection is renamed or when `sync_enabled` is toggled, because both are stored on the underlying connection record. An update revalidates its ETag a second time after the round trip to Databricks, so a concurrent write that lands mid-request is refused rather than silently overwritten.

### Rotating credentials

`credentials` is only re-sent when the configured values change, so an apply that renames the connection does not rotate the stored secret or make SELECT reconnect. Rotation is atomic: `client_id` and `client_secret` move together, because SELECT has no way to change one without the other.

SELECT never returns either value, so a change made outside Terraform is invisible to a refresh.

### Connection names must be unique

A connection name has to be unique among an organization's Databricks connections. SELECT does not currently translate that constraint into a helpful error — a duplicate name fails the apply with an opaque `HTTP 500` rather than a conflict naming the field.

### Deleting a connection is not reversible

Destroying this resource removes the connection and the usage data SELECT has collected through it. Re-adding the same account and workspace starts its history over.
